name: District of Columbia

context: DC ESC Manual: stabilize swales, ditches, perimeter slopes and slopes steeper than 3:1 within 7 days; other disturbed areas within 14 days.
DC ESC Manual: where wind erosion is expected, install RECPs over the compost blanket regardless of slope.
cover_rules: DC temporary seeding: oats are the recommended nurse crop for warm-season grasses; use 1/3 of the listed rate as a nurse crop.
seeding: DC temporary seeding: warm-season grass rates are pounds of pure live seed (PLS); adjust for germination and purity.
DC seeding: plant warm-season native mixes with a regular grass drill; indiangrass and bluestems need a specialized native seed drill.
disturbed: DC ESC: stabilize slopes steeper than 3:1 and swales within 7 days of disturbance; other graded areas within 14 days.
DC ESC: use RECPs over compost blanket where high winds and wind erosion are expected.

coverPlant.text: DC temporary seeding: cool-season grasses Feb. 15 to Apr. 30; Aug. 15 to Nov. 30.
DC temporary seeding: warm-season millets May 1 to Aug. 14.

seedWin.text: DC temporary seeding, millets: May 1 to Aug. 14.
DC temporary seeding, cool-season grasses: Feb. 15 to Apr. 30; Aug. 15 to Nov. 30.

gaps: No eFOTG files for DC; no NRCS DC wind-erosion practice standards found.
No cropland, residue, windbreak, grazing or CRP guidance found; DC has almost no farmland.
Cereal grain temporary rates in the DC manual table were not cleanly readable, so omitted.
